findings.statement: OBLIGATION 1 (atomically bind one spawned agent_id to one run, assignment and digest) is DISCHARGED on current bytes, within the stated per-run scope. ESTABLISHED BY REPRODUCTION, NOT ACCEPTED ON ASSERTION: I rebuilt the concurrency experiment on a private sandbox copy of the HEAD bytes and measured 0 breaches in 60 independent two-way trials (one agent_id, two agent-unbound receipts, two genuinely simultaneous stops) and 0 breaches in 15 four-way trials. The measurement is a real detector, not a hope: mutating only 'fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)' out of acquire_agent_lock in the sandbox copy re-opened the race at 22/30 trials (73%), so a defect of the reported magnitude would survive 60 clean trials with probability ~0.27**60. Path coverage is closed by construction, not by sampling: 'event: consumed' ledger rows and receipt 'state: consumed' are written at exactly two places in the tree (subagent_stop_validate.py lines 698-726), both inside consume_under_agent_lock, which is only ever reached from the try/finally that holds the lock; no other module in .codex/hooks or .agent-harness/scripts writes either. Lock-unavailability is fail-closed on all four shapes I could construct - lock directory uncreatable (parent 0500) -> block/PermissionError; lock FILE uncreatable (.agent-locks 0500) -> block/PermissionError; .agent-locks path pre-existing as a regular file -> block/FileExistsError; .agent-locks a symlink -> block 'the agent lock directory is a symlink'. In every one the receipt stayed 'open' and zero consume rows were appended. SCOPE, stated rather than glossed: the ceiling is one assignment per agent_id PER RUN. One agent_id consuming in two different runs is deliberately permitted and fixture-pinned (test_one_agent_bound_in_one_run_is_still_admissible_in_another), so the literal words 'bound to one run' are delivered as 'bound to one assignment within each run it stops in'.

findings.statement: OBLIGATION 2 (make receipt/lease creation failure a hard Start failure) is NOT DISCHARGED. The round-6 fix is real but partial, and I reproduced the obligation-2 case still passing at Start on current bytes. describe_admission_receipt consults the admission LEDGER only inside 'if not matches:' (subagent_start_context.py:320-359), i.e. only when the receipt scan finds ZERO receipt files for this agent_id. One receipt for a DIFFERENT assignment therefore masks the orphan. REPRODUCED end to end through the real CLI and the real hook: (1) admit_agent.py --assignment-id A --expect-agent-id G against a 0500 admissions directory -> exit 1, no receipt on disk, orphan 'minted' row for A naming G; (2) admit_agent.py --assignment-id B --expect-agent-id G after the directory is writable again -> SUCCEEDS, because other_assignment_bound_to_agent scans receipt FILES and A's never landed; (3) SubagentStart for agent_id G -> 'Admission receipt: open, bound to assignment A-HOOK-FIXTURE-2' and 'Hook preflight: PASS'. A receipt creation failure for this exact agent_id occurred and Start reported PASS - the same proof shape round 6 used to reject the previous version. Worse, the code contradicts its OWN written rule: the module docstring states the fatal condition as "the ledger's *latest* minted/reopened row for some assignment names this agent_id, and no consumed row for that assignment follows it -> hard FAIL". That condition holds in the reproduction and the rule is never evaluated, because the ledger read is short-circuited. This is the fourth instance of the pattern the assignment asks me to weigh: a stated rule broader than the code that implements it.

findings.statement: OBLIGATION 2, second undischarged path: the Start-time rule is structurally inoperative for --agent-id-unknown mints, and nothing on disk or in the record says so. admit_agent.py writes expected_agent_id='' on a token-only receipt AND on its ledger row; orphaned_mint_assignment_ids matches on 'expected == agent_id' with agent_id constrained non-empty by ADMISSION_KEY_RE, so a token-only mint can never match. REPRODUCED: --agent-id-unknown mint against a 0500 admissions directory -> exit 1, no receipt, orphan ledger row {event: minted, expected_agent_id: '', agent_binding: 'token-only'}; SubagentStart for the spawned agent -> 'Admission receipt: none found' / 'Hook preflight: PASS'. Unlike F-R7-02 this one is not obviously fixable at Start (there is no agent id to key on at mint time), so the honest disposition is a STATED scope limit. It is not stated anywhere I could find: admit_agent.py's --agent-id-unknown docstring carefully enumerates what is DELIVERED and NOT DELIVERED for obligation 1 in that mode and says nothing about obligation 2, and subagent_start_context.py's three-state rule is written as universal. Given that this review's recurring failure has twice been the RECORD rather than the code, an undocumented mode in which the newly-claimed Start check silently does not run is a record defect in its own right.

findings.statement: OBLIGATION 4 (pass a replacement live overlapping-run canary with unique write attribution) is NOT DISCHARGED ON CURRENT BYTES: C5 has gone stale in the same class of defect that sank C1 and C4 - the artifact describes something other than what is being judged. C5's own attestation pins stop_hook_sha256=dc19da4d43b84e459c3b5a5a4ee5abbc94726ca83b7246f85364c29b820fda93 and head_commit=d94270f. I verified: 'git show d94270f:.codex/hooks/subagent_stop_validate.py | sha256sum' reproduces that digest exactly, and the file at HEAD cef6f00 hashes to 0533da884250e03e91670aa458e3915859d91b31fc856fa72537dae65a966625. So the attestation self-identifies a scope that excludes the bytes under judgement. subagent_start_context.py, admit_agent.py and validate_harness.py have all changed since d94270f as well. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, precisely: C5 passed, and passed cleanly, against d94270f - the 39 ms ACTIVE_RUN bracket names the decoy at both ends, the lease named the canary run, expected_agent_id was enforced, consumed_by_agent_id=d070-canary-c5, and the result digest is pinned in the append-only ledger; the containment analysis is honest about second-resolution stamps rather than overclaiming. MITIGATION, stated so the adjudicator can weigh it rather than take my word: 'git diff --numstat d94270f..cef6f00' on the stop hook is '185 0' - 185 insertions and ZERO deletions - so every line C5 exercised is still present, in order, and the change is the addition of the agent-lock gate plus a pure extraction of the consume body into consume_under_agent_lock at unchanged indentation. The risk that C5's property silently broke is therefore low. But 'low risk by inspection of a diff' is exactly the standard rounds 4 and 5 refused for C1 and C4, and the newly inserted code sits UPSTREAM of the consume C5 attested, gating it. findings.statement: SEMANTICS OF 'HARD START FAILURE', recorded so obligation 2 is not read as more than it is. SubagentStart's only output channel is _common.emit_additional_context, which prints hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext plus an optional systemMessage. There is no decision/block or permission-deny field, unlike SubagentStop's block(). A 'hard Start failure' therefore means the injected bootstrap line reads 'Hook preflight: FAIL - ...' and a systemMessage warning is emitted; it does NOT abort or refuse the subagent. Under the recorded LOCAL-ADAPT (VS Code does not dispatch project Start/Stop hooks, so the parent invokes them explicitly) even that text only reaches the agent if the parent chooses to inject it. What actually makes the system fail-closed is SubagentStop, which does block. I record this as inconclusive rather than as a finding because D-065's wording is about the Start hook's verdict and the code does now carry that verdict load-bearingly, and because the audit report already says so ('load-bearing in Hook preflight: PASS|FAIL'). But an adjudicator reading 'hard Start failure' as 'the agent is prevented from running' would be reading more than the mechanism delivers.

findings.statement: ON THE STATED SAME-OS-USER RESIDUAL, which the assignment places out of scope as a finding but asks me to weigh: it does NOT by itself prevent obligations 1 and 3 from being honestly called discharged, provided the discharge is stated in the same breath as the residual. The obligations are confusion-class properties - prompt substitution, same-run mix-up, pointer races, unattributable writes - and every mechanism I verified delivers them against an honest or merely buggy path. The residual is recorded in three independent places I checked (admit_agent.py's THREAT MODEL block, the audit report's table last row and section 2 preamble, and the shared context pack's Q-HOOK-01 remediation row), and each says forgery is 'still possible' rather than eliminated. That is the correct disposition and it is not being laundered. The honest caveat is on the word 'atomically' in obligation 1: the mutual exclusion is atomic against concurrent stops, not against an agent that writes the ledger or a receipt directly, and no reading of the delivered mechanism should be allowed to blur those.

findings.statement: OVERALL VERDICT: the four-item F-D065-01 remedy is NOT DISCHARGED on HEAD cef6f00. Per item - obligation 1 DISCHARGED (0/60 and 0/15 breaches on HEAD bytes, 22/30 with the lock mutated out, all four lock-failure shapes fail closed, no consume path outside the lock); obligation 2 NOT DISCHARGED (F-R7-02 reproduces a receipt-creation failure for a named agent_id that SubagentStart reports as PASS, and the code contradicts its own stated three-state rule; F-R7-03 records a second, undocumented inoperative path); obligation 3 DISCHARGED (12/12 mutants killed, 74 -> 102 fixtures verified independently, no vacuous fixtures found); obligation 4 NOT DISCHARGED ON CURRENT BYTES (C5's attestation pins the stop hook at d94270f; HEAD differs, +185/-0). Round 7 is the third consecutive round in which the defect found is one the accompanying prose already claimed was handled - here subagent_start_context.py's docstring states a three-state rule the function does not evaluate when the agent holds any other receipt. That is the same failure mode as R4's two false report claims and R6's false justification, at one further remove: not a false claim about the past, but a rule written as universal and implemented as conditional. I recommend the gate NOT be flipped, and that obligation 2's fix be accompanied by a fixture that starts from a NON-empty receipt scan, since every existing obligation-2 fixture starts from an empty one.
